edits.find: According to digital publishing benchmarks, newsletter subscribers in high-intent verticals—such as software engineering, enterprise technology, personal finance, and corporate leadership—demonstrate significantly higher lifetime customer value (LTV). edits.find:
• Unique Open Rate (Target: 35% – 50%+): Measures the percentage of delivered emails opened by unique recipients. While Apple's Mail Privacy Protection (MPP) can inflate aggregate open figures, tracking relative trends helps gauge headline effectiveness and list health.
  • Click-Through Rate (CTR: 3% – 8%): The percentage of delivered recipients who clicked at least one link. High CTR reflects strong contextual alignment and high subscriber intent.
  • Monthly Churn Rate (Target: < 3% – 5%): The proportion of paid subscribers who cancel their subscription within a given month. In paid subscription businesses, keeping monthly churn below 4% is critical; higher churn creates a "leaky bucket" requiring unsustainable acquisition spending.
edits.replace:
• Unique Open Rate: Measures the percentage of delivered emails opened by unique recipients. Because Apple's Mail Privacy Protection (MPP) can inflate open figures, compare your own trends over time rather than chasing a fixed target.
  • Click-Through Rate (CTR): The percentage of delivered recipients who clicked at least one link. A rising CTR suggests your content and links match what readers want.
  • Monthly Churn Rate: The proportion of paid subscribers who cancel within a given month. High churn creates a "leaky bucket" that forces you to keep spending on acquisition just to stand still.
edits.reason: Removed unsourced KPI target ranges
